title: Atomic movies of elementary chemical steps without a photo-trigger

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a reliable way to reconstruct the ordered atomic changes of an elementary chemical step initiated by substrate addition, heat, voltage or another non-photochemical trigger. It would produce a time-ordered series of electron-density maps with enough spatial and effective temporal resolution to distinguish the relevant structures and establish their sequence. The measured chemistry would also need to represent the intended reaction, rather than a different pathway imposed by crystallization or experimental conditions. This is a proposed capability whose defining advance is broad access to validated elementary-step sequences.

An atomic movie in this context is a reconstruction from diffraction measurements collected at different reaction delays, often across many crystals. Each map can contain overlapping populations of reactants, intermediates and products. Establishing a chemical sequence therefore requires population analysis, structural refinement and mechanistic interpretation; a succession of maps does not automatically identify a unique pathway. Selected mixing-triggered enzyme measurements already provide part of this capability, so the frontier concerns breadth, temporal resolution and interpretability rather than the first observation of any non-photoactive reaction.

significance.text: If achieved across diverse reaction classes, this capability would connect measured reaction kinetics to experimentally resolved structural sequences. It could reveal intermediate geometries and the structural changes associated with bond rearrangements in non-photoactive enzymes and crystalline chemical systems, on the timescales relevant to their chemistry. Existing mixing-triggered enzyme experiments and photo-triggered framework experiments provide concrete foundations for that conditional advance.

The movie analogy has important limits. Diffraction measures ensemble information, and inferred structures can depend on kinetic models, occupancy estimates and extrapolation. Even an atomic-resolution electron-density series would not automatically show proton transfer: assigning hydrogen positions and proton movement would require adequate hydrogen sensitivity and complementary evidence. The scientific gain would be stronger experimental constraints on mechanisms, with uncertainty retained wherever competing pathways explain the observations.

Conditional downstream possibilities include more informed catalyst design and better explanations of how temperature, substrate delivery or electrical conditions alter a reaction. These are reasoned possibilities, not demonstrated consequences of the proposed innovation. A structural sequence would not by itself deliver a better catalyst, establish that the same pathway operates outside the crystal, or make every chemical reaction experimentally accessible.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central missing capability is a broadly transferable combination of reaction initiation, synchronization, diffraction sampling and structural interpretation that resolves non-photoinitiated elementary chemistry on its own timescale. Reaction timing must be sufficiently well defined across the illuminated volume and across serial specimens. Nominal exposure duration or a short delivery transit time alone does not establish effective reaction-time resolution. The supplied evidence demonstrates selected implementations, but does not establish access to arbitrary elementary steps.

Substrate delivery introduces system-dependent diffusion and population problems: molecules may reach different regions of a crystal at different times, leaving several reaction states superimposed in the diffraction data. Collecting additional delays is useful only if those populations can be separated well enough to identify and order the chemistry. The xylose-isomerase study explicitly describes difficulty interpreting overlapping states from electron density alone, illustrating the gap between observing turnover-associated changes and uniquely resolving an elementary step.

Irreversible chemistry complicates repeated measurements because a specimen cannot necessarily be reset for another reaction cycle. This does not mean that every irreversible reaction physically destroys its crystal. Serial crystallography already addresses this limitation by measuring fresh specimens, but extending the approach requires reproducible reaction preparation and sufficiently complete diffraction data from comparable populations.

Further engineering questions concern synchronized electrical initiation and rapid thermal initiation across specimens. These remain targets identified by the concept; the supplied review does not establish their detailed limitations or current performance. Preparing a crystal at a selected temperature and then adding substrate must be distinguished from abruptly triggering a reaction with a temperature change. Likewise, whether lattice constraints alter motions or pathways relevant to solution or surface chemistry requires reaction-specific validation rather than a blanket assumption.

current_state.text: The July 2025 multi-temperature serial-crystallography study demonstrated substrate-triggered turnover measurements for CTX-M-14 β-lactamase at 20, 30 and 37 °C, using a 3 s delay. For xylose isomerase, the reported reaction measurements covered 20–50 °C with 60 s delays, with additional 180 s measurements at 20 and 50 °C. These are selected non-photoactive enzyme achievements. They establish temperature-dependent turnover measurements, but do not by themselves establish elementary-step resolution on arbitrary reaction timescales.

The same apparatus supported environmental-control ranges of 7–55 °C and 50 °C to above 70 °C through separate modules. Thus, the broad description of operation from below 10 °C to above 70 °C concerns apparatus capability; turnover was not demonstrated throughout that range. These experiments used substrate addition at controlled temperatures, which does not establish rapid temperature-jump initiation.

The 2024 metal–organic-framework study reported photoinduced CO dissociation and structural dynamics in PCN–224(Fe)–CO, initiated by a 400 nm femtosecond laser pulse. It obtained electron-density maps across many delays and used kinetic and structural analysis to interpret the evolving species. Its reported novelty was the extension of time-resolved serial femtosecond crystallography to a non-protein chemical crystal; the paper acknowledged earlier static chemical serial femtosecond crystallography. It therefore supplies an important photo-triggered precedent, rather than a demonstration of the proposed non-photochemical capability.

The reconciled research attributes millisecond mixing, a below-2-ms synchrotron example and a shortage of suitable reaction-triggering tools to the July 2024 ACS Catalysis review. No text or artifact from that source was retained in the supplied evidence, so these particular assertions cannot be checked here. They remain unresolved rather than disproved and should not be treated as established timing benchmarks. The separately mentioned 0.5 ms droplet flight time does not establish sub-2-ms effective reaction resolution.

The supplied review was based on complete retained article text for the two Nature studies, together with supplementary and peer-review material used for the enzyme study. Its assessment concerned the textual reports; figures and electron-density-map images were not visually inspected. The dated demonstrations are therefore supported at the level described in that review. However, the freshness record is empty, so these inputs cannot establish whether a general thermal or electrochemical elementary-step capability remained unavailable as of November 1, 2026. That gap does not invalidate the reported 2024 and 2025 achievements.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed breadth demonstration: measure three chemically unrelated non-photoactive reactions, including at least one small-molecule or heterogeneous catalytic step, with each reaction initiated without a photochemical trigger. For every case, obtain maps at enough delays, spatial resolution and effective temporal resolution to identify and order the elementary step. Three reactions would demonstrate a specified breadth of applicability, not literal universality. This is a proposed benchmark, not an established community standard.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed breadth demonstration

completion_criteria.text: Proposed measurement requirements: pre-register the spatial-resolution target, effective timing uncertainty, temporal sampling, population-separation requirements and acceptable uncertainty in structural assignments. Demonstrate that the data distinguish the claimed sequence from plausible alternative sequences or mixtures. Repeat the measurements across independent sample preparations and make the diffraction data, timing characterization and analysis sufficiently available for independent reanalysis and reproduction. One trapped intermediate or one photo-pumped oscillation would not satisfy the proposed scope.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed measurement requirements

completion_criteria.text: Proposed fidelity requirements: compare orthogonal kinetics and mechanism-sensitive measurements inside and outside the lattice within pre-registered tolerances appropriate to each reaction. Matching overall rates alone would not establish an unchanged mechanism. The supplied peer-review discussion notes that crystal and solution reaction rates can differ; this is expert context motivating a fidelity check, rather than a comparative kinetic result established by that study.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed fidelity requirements

completion_criteria.text: Proposed practical boundaries: report which crystal forms, specimen sizes, trigger conditions, reaction rates and irreversible sampling requirements are compatible with the method, together with failures and unresolved assignments. If proton transfer is claimed, include evidence sufficient to support hydrogen-sensitive interpretation. Completion would mean reproducible elementary-step movies within clearly demonstrated operating conditions, with broader applicability remaining a question for further experiments.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed practical boundaries

related_concepts.text: Roster-based distinction: CRX-12, “Continuous atomic-resolution crystallography inside working devices and static extreme environments,” overlaps through measurements under applied conditions, including electrical operation. CRX-06 specifically requires identifying and ordering elementary chemical changes; continuous device diffraction alone need not provide that assignment. Conversely, a triggered reaction sequence need not involve a continuously operating device. The two entries retain separate goals.

Roster-based distinction: CRX-08, “Ab initio atomic structure of matter that exists only once,” concerns structure recovery when the target exists only once. CRX-06 can consume many fresh specimens while reconstructing a reproducible reaction sequence, so destructive or irreversible sampling is compatible with it. CRX-01, “Atomic-resolution imaging of a single non-crystalline molecule before destruction,” shares the challenge of obtaining information before specimen loss, but targets an individual non-crystalline molecule rather than a crystallographic reaction series.

Roster-based distinction: CRX-09, “Protonation state as a routine crystallographic observable,” would strengthen CRX-06 where proton positions or transfers determine the mechanism. Ordering a reaction structurally and establishing its protonation changes remain distinct achievements. CRX-04, “Atomic ensembles measured from total X-ray scattering,” shares the problem of interpreting structural populations, while its defining measurement target differs from resolving a triggered elementary-step sequence.

Roster-based distinction: CRX-11, “Diffraction-quality crystals of arbitrary macromolecules on demand,” could broaden access to suitable enzyme specimens, while CRX-10, “Laboratory sources that do facility-class coherent X-ray crystallography,” could broaden access to enabling instrumentation. Neither goal alone supplies synchronized reaction initiation or reliable elementary-step assignment. These are potential enabling relationships, not reasons to merge the entries.

The research connects this concept to an earlier historical item seeking a movie of any reaction. That item's original wording and scope were not supplied. It can therefore be retained only as a reported motivation; the present concept's identity rests on broad, validated access to elementary steps initiated without a photochemical trigger.

change_log.change: Preserved CRX-06 and its title while defining the target as broad, validated elementary-step resolution without photochemical initiation.
change_log.reason: Selected mixing-triggered enzyme measurements already exist; the innovation cannot be framed as the first access to all non-photoactive chemistry.

change_log.change: Explained that atomic movies are ensemble reconstructions requiring population separation, refinement and mechanistic interpretation.
change_log.reason: The reviewed studies describe overlapping states and model-dependent structural assignments, so maps alone do not establish a unique reaction sequence.

change_log.change: Replaced the claimed full-range turnover demonstration with the actual enzyme temperatures and reaction delays, separately retaining the apparatus operating ranges.
change_log.reason: Environmental-control capability from below 10 °C to above 70 °C was conflated with narrower demonstrated reaction conditions.

change_log.change: Distinguished substrate initiation at controlled temperature from rapid thermal triggering.
change_log.reason: The multi-temperature enzyme measurements do not establish temperature-jump initiation.

change_log.change: Narrowed the 2024 framework novelty claim to time-resolved serial femtosecond crystallography of a non-protein chemical crystal.
change_log.reason: The study acknowledged earlier static chemical serial femtosecond crystallography.

change_log.change: Retained the ACS timing and triggering assertions as unresolved, without presenting them as verified benchmarks.
change_log.reason: The ACS source has no retained text; a short droplet flight time also does not establish effective reaction-time resolution.

change_log.change: Reframed irreversible chemistry as a specimen-reset limitation that serial methods can address.
change_log.reason: Irreversibility does not necessarily physically destroy a crystal or prevent measurements using fresh specimens.

change_log.change: Qualified proton-transfer observability and downstream catalyst improvements.
change_log.reason: Atomic-resolution electron density does not automatically establish hydrogen motion, and better catalysts require additional evidence and development.

change_log.change: Expanded the proposed completion demonstration to include effective timing, population identifiability, uncertainty, reproducibility and mechanism-sensitive fidelity checks.
change_log.reason: Matching overall kinetics alone cannot establish mechanistic equivalence, and finite demonstrations establish breadth rather than universality.

change_log.change: Used the supplied roster titles to clarify overlaps while preserving separate entries.
change_log.reason: The roster supplies identity-level context that was unavailable to the reviewer, but does not supply detailed specifications for the other concepts.

change_log.change: Preserved textual-review, visual-inspection and freshness limitations.
change_log.reason: The supplied evidence supports dated achievements without establishing a comprehensive field-wide frontier as of November 1, 2026.

unresolved_issues: The supplied freshness record cannot establish the field-wide availability or absence of general non-photoinitiated elementary-step movies as of November 1, 2026.
The ACS Catalysis source must be captured and checked to resolve the attributed triggering limitation, millisecond mixing performance and below-2-ms synchrotron claim.
The supplied evidence does not establish the current performance limits of synchronized electrical or rapid thermal initiation across serial specimens.
Lattice fidelity, including possible changes to solution or surface reaction pathways, requires reaction-specific evidence.
Numerical acceptance thresholds for spatial resolution, effective temporal resolution, population separation and fidelity remain to be defined for the proposed demonstration.
The original wording of historical item 4 remains unavailable, and related-concept comparisons are limited to the supplied roster titles.
The source review did not visually inspect figures or electron-density maps; its structural assessment rests on the retained textual reports.
